title: Fractions: The Four Operations and Word Problems
seo_title: Fractions – Primary 6 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions and mixed numbers; compare and order fractions; solve word problems involving fractions. (summary of the NERDC Primary 6 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 maths worksheets on fractions: comparing and ordering, adding and subtracting with unlike denominators, multiplying and dividing fractions and mixed numbers, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Common denominator to add; reciprocal to divide
key_sub: Change mixed numbers to improper fractions first.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • To add or subtract, change to a common denominator (use the LCM).
  • To multiply, multiply the numerators and the denominators. To divide, multiply by the reciprocal of the second fraction.
  • In word problems, find what the whole is first, then the fraction of it, or the fraction that is left.

Examples

Example

2 1/3 ÷ 1 3/4

7/3 ÷ 7/4 = 7/3 × 4/7

Answer: 4/3 = 1 1/3

Example

Ade spent 2/5 of ₦5,000

5,000 ÷ 5 × 2

Answer: ₦2,000

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Dividing without changing mixed numbersChange them to improper fractions first.
Finding the fraction of what is left from the wholeRead the question: 'of the remainder' means of what is left.
Not simplifyingGive answers in their lowest terms.

faq.q: Why does dividing by a fraction give a bigger answer?
faq.a: You are finding how many small parts fit.

items.q: Which letter shows 74?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. 74 = 1 34: go to 1, then 3 more marks. That is letter D.

items.q: Which letter shows 1 23?
items.e: Each whole is split into 3 equal parts, so each mark is 13. Count 1 whole, then 2 more marks. That is letter C.

items.q: Which letter shows 2 14?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. Count 2 wholes, then 1 more mark. That is letter B.

items.q: Which letter shows 75?
items.e: Each whole is split into 5 equal parts, so each mark is 15. 75 = 1 25: go to 1, then 2 more marks. That is letter A.

items.q: Which letter shows 116?
items.e: Each whole is split into 6 equal parts, so each mark is 16. 116 = 1 56: go to 1, then 5 more marks. That is letter B.

items.q: Which fraction is the greatest?
items.e: Write them all with the denominator 24: 34 = 1824, 58 = 1524, 23 = 1624, 712 = 1424. The greatest is 1824, so the answer is 34.

items.q: Which fraction is the smallest?
items.e: Write them all with the denominator 36: 56 = 3036, 79 = 2836, 34 = 2736, 23 = 2436. The smallest is 2436, so the answer is 23.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: All four are between 1 and 2. Look at how much each one is short of 2: 74 = 1 34 (14 short), 1 23 (13 short), 95 = 1 45 (15 short), 1 58 (38 short). The smallest gap is 15, so 95 is the greatest.

items.q: Which fraction is between 12 and 34?
items.e: In eighths: 12 = 48 and 34 = 68. 58 is between them. 78 and 45 are more than 34, and 38 is less than 12.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
23, 56, 712
c: 712, 23, 56
712, 56, 23
56, 23, 712
23, 56, 712
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 23 = 812, 56 = 1012, 712 = 712. So the order is 712, 23, 56.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
35, 12, 710
c: 12, 35, 710
35, 12, 710
710, 35, 12
35, 710, 12
items.e: Use the common denominator 10: 35 = 610, 12 = 510, 710 = 710. So the order is 12, 35, 710.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
32, 54, 1 13
c: 32, 1 13, 54
1 13, 32, 54
32, 54, 1 13
54, 1 13, 32
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 32 = 1812, 54 = 1512, 1 13 = 1612. So the order is 54, 1 13, 32.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
94, 2 13, 136
c: 136, 94, 2 13
94, 136, 2 13
94, 2 13, 136
2 13, 94, 136
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 94 = 2712, 2 13 = 2812, 136 = 2612. So the order is 136, 94, 2 13.

items.q: Which statement is true?
c: 49 > 35
18 > 16
54 < 1 13
23 = 34
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 54 = 1512 and 1 13 = 1612. So 54 < 1 13 is true.

items.q: Which letter shows 74?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. 74 = 1 34: go to 1, then 3 more marks. That is letter C.

items.q: Which letter shows 1 23?
items.e: Each whole is split into 3 equal parts, so each mark is 13. Count 1 whole, then 2 more marks. That is letter A.

items.q: Which letter shows 2 14?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. Count 2 wholes, then 1 more mark. That is letter D.

items.q: Which letter shows 75?
items.e: Each whole is split into 5 equal parts, so each mark is 15. 75 = 1 25: go to 1, then 2 more marks. That is letter B.

items.q: Which letter shows 116?
items.e: Each whole is split into 6 equal parts, so each mark is 16. 116 = 1 56: go to 1, then 5 more marks. That is letter D.

items.q: Which letter shows 74?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. 74 = 1 34: go to 1, then 3 more marks. That is letter B.

items.q: What is the lowest common denominator of 23 and 34?
items.e: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12. Multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12. The first number in both lists is 12.

items.q: What is the lowest common denominator of 14 and 16?
items.e: Multiples of 6: 6, 12. Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12. The first number in both lists is 12. 4 × 6 = 24 also works, but it is not the lowest.

items.q: What is the lowest common denominator of 38 and 56?
items.e: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24. The first number in both lists is 24. 8 × 6 = 48 also works, but it is not the lowest.

items.q: The green part is 23 and the yellow part is 14. The dashed lines split both bars into twelfths. Which shows both fractions in twelfths?
c: 812 and 312
212 and 112
1112 and 912
612 and 412
items.e: Count the small parts in each shaded piece. 3 × 4 = 12, so multiply the numerator and denominator of 23 by 4: 812. 4 × 3 = 12, so multiply the numerator and denominator of 14 by 3: 312. The answer is 812 and 312.

items.q: The green part is 12 and the yellow part is 25. The dashed lines split both bars into tenths. Which shows both fractions in tenths?
c: 510 and 410
110 and 210
910 and 710
210 and 1010
items.e: Count the small parts in each shaded piece. 2 × 5 = 10, so multiply the numerator and denominator of 12 by 5: 510. 5 × 2 = 10, so multiply the numerator and denominator of 25 by 2: 410. The answer is 510 and 410.

items.q: Tunde wrote 12 + 13 = 25. What mistake did he make?
c: He added the numerators and the denominators
items.e: Halves and thirds are different sizes, so you cannot add the numerators and the denominators. Use sixths: 36 + 26 = 56. Also, 25 is less than 12, so it cannot be the total.

items.q:
23 + 14 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 4 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 23 = 812 and 14 = 312. Add the numerators: 812 + 312 = 1112. The answer is 1112.

items.q:
15 + 12 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 5 and 2 is 10, so use 10 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 15 = 210 and 12 = 510. Add the numerators: 210 + 510 = 710. The answer is 710.

items.q:
14 + 16 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 14 = 312 and 16 = 212. Add the numerators: 312 + 212 = 512. The answer is 512.

items.q:
13 + 25 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 5 is 15, so use 15 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 13 = 515 and 25 = 615. Add the numerators: 515 + 615 = 1115. The answer is 1115.

items.q:
2 13 + 1 14 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 4 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 2 13 = 2 412 and 1 14 = 1 312. Add the fractions: 412 + 312 = 712. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 1 = 3. The answer is 3 712.

items.q:
1 12 + 2 15 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 2 and 5 is 10, so use 10 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 1 12 = 1 510 and 2 15 = 2 210. Add the fractions: 510 + 210 = 710. Add the whole numbers: 1 + 2 = 3. The answer is 3 710.

items.q:
3 16 + 1 12 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: 6 is a multiple of 2, so use 6 as the common denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 1 12 = 1 36. Add the fractions: 16 + 36 = 46. Add the whole numbers: 3 + 1 = 4. Simplify: divide the numerator and denominator of 46 by 2 to get 23. The answer is 4 23.

items.q:
2 38 + 4 14 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: 8 is a multiple of 4, so use 8 as the common denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 4 14 = 4 28. Add the fractions: 38 + 28 = 58. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 4 = 6. The answer is 6 58.

items.q:
1 16 + 2 34 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 6 and 4 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 1 16 = 1 212 and 2 34 = 2 912. Add the fractions: 212 + 912 = 1112. Add the whole numbers: 1 + 2 = 3. The answer is 3 1112.

items.q:
2 13 + 1 34 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 4 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 2 13 = 2 412 and 1 34 = 1 912. Add the fractions: 412 + 912 = 1312. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 1 = 3. 1312 is an improper fraction: 1312 = 1 112. 3 + 1 112 = 4 112. The answer is 4 112.

items.q:
2 56 + 1 12 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: 6 is a multiple of 2, so use 6 as the common denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 1 12 = 1 36. Add the fractions: 56 + 36 = 86. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 1 = 3. 86 is an improper fraction: 86 = 1 26. 3 + 1 26 = 4 26. Simplify: divide the numerator and denominator of 26 by 2 to get 13. The answer is 4 13.

items.q:
3 45 + 1 12 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 5 and 2 is 10, so use 10 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 3 45 = 3 810 and 1 12 = 1 510. Add the fractions: 810 + 510 = 1310. Add the whole numbers: 3 + 1 = 4. 1310 is an improper fraction: 1310 = 1 310. 4 + 1 310 = 5 310. The answer is 5 310.

items.q:
1 78 + 2 14 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: 8 is a multiple of 4, so use 8 as the common denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 2 14 = 2 28. Add the fractions: 78 + 28 = 98. Add the whole numbers: 1 + 2 = 3. 98 is an improper fraction: 98 = 1 18. 3 + 1 18 = 4 18. The answer is 4 18.

items.q:
2 34 + 3 56 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 2 34 = 2 912 and 3 56 = 3 1012. Add the fractions: 912 + 1012 = 1912. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 3 = 5. 1912 is an improper fraction: 1912 = 1 712. 5 + 1 712 = 6 712. The answer is 6 712.

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 35?
items.e: Swap the numerator and the denominator: the reciprocal of 35 is 53. Check: 35 × 53 = 1515 = 1.

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 17?
items.e: Swap the numerator and the denominator: 17 becomes 71 = 7. Check: 17 × 7 = 1.

items.q: Which multiplication has the same answer as 23 ÷ 57?
c: 23 × 75
32 × 57
23 × 57
32 × 75
items.e: Keep the first fraction and multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor 57, which is 75: 23 × 75. Do not flip 23.

items.q: Which multiplication has the same answer as 49 ÷ 16?
c: 94 × 16
49 × 16
items.e: Keep the first fraction and multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor 16, which is 6: 49 × 6. Do not flip 49.

items.q:
The bar shows 23. How many groups of 16 are there in 23?
23 ÷ 16 = ?
items.e: Count in sixths: 23 = 46. Each group is 1 sixth. 4 sixths make 4 ÷ 1 = 4 groups. So 23 ÷ 16 = 4. Check: 4 × 16 = 23.

items.q:
The bar shows 34. How many groups of 38 are there in 34?
34 ÷ 38 = ?
items.e: Count in eighths: 34 = 68. Each group is 3 eighths. 6 eighths make 6 ÷ 3 = 2 groups. So 34 ÷ 38 = 2. Check: 2 × 38 = 34.

items.q:
The bar shows 56. How many groups of 13 are there in 56?
56 ÷ 13 = ?
items.e: Count in sixths: 13 = 26. Each group is 2 sixths. 5 sixths make 2 full groups, with 1 sixth left over. That 1 sixth is 12 of a group. So 56 ÷ 13 = 2 12. Check: 2 12 × 13 = 56.

items.q:
12 ÷ 34 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 34 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 43: 12 ÷ 34 = 12 × 43. Cancel common factors first: divide 4 and 2 by 2. Now 1 × 23 = 23. Check: 23 × 34 = 12.

items.q:
25 ÷ 45 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 45 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 54: 25 ÷ 45 = 25 × 54. Cancel common factors first: divide 2 and 4 by 2, and the 5s cancel. Now 1 × 12 = 12. Check: 12 × 45 = 25.

items.q:
67 ÷ 27 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 27 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 72: 67 ÷ 27 = 67 × 72. Cancel common factors first: divide 6 and 2 by 2, and the 7s cancel. Now 3 × 1 = 3. Check: 3 × 27 = 67.

items.q:
56 ÷ 5 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The numerator 5 can be divided by 5: 5 ÷ 5 = 1. Keep the denominator: 56 ÷ 5 = 16. Check: 16 × 5 = 56.

items.q:
4 ÷ 27 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 27 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 72: 4 ÷ 27 = 4 × 72. Cancel common factors first: divide 4 and 2 by 2. Now 2 × 7 = 14. Check: 14 × 27 = 4.

items.q:
35 ÷ 910 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 910 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 109: 35 ÷ 910 = 35 × 109. Cancel common factors first: divide 3 and 9 by 3, and divide 10 and 5 by 5. Now 1 × 23 = 23. Check: 23 × 910 = 35.

items.q:
910 ÷ 6 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 6 is the same as multiplying by 16: 910 ÷ 6 = 910 × 16 = 960. Simplify: 960 = 320. Check: 320 × 6 = 1820 = 910.

items.q:
12 ÷ 34 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 34 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 43: 12 ÷ 34 = 12 × 43. Cancel common factors first: divide 12 and 3 by 3. Now 4 × 4 = 16. Check: 16 × 34 = 12.

items.q:
29 ÷ 56 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 56 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 65: 29 ÷ 56 = 29 × 65. Cancel common factors first: divide 6 and 9 by 3. Now 23 × 25 = 415. Check: 415 × 56 = 29.

items.q:
611 ÷ 322 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 322 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 223: 611 ÷ 322 = 611 × 223. Cancel common factors first: divide 6 and 3 by 3, and divide 22 and 11 by 11. Now 2 × 2 = 4. Check: 4 × 322 = 611.

items.q:
3 ÷ 49 = ?
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 49 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 94: 3 ÷ 49 = 3 × 94 = 3 × 91 × 4 = 274 = 6 34. Check: 6 34 × 49 = 3.

items.q:
512 ÷ 10 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 10 is the same as multiplying by 110: 512 ÷ 10 = 512 × 110 = 5120. Simplify: 5120 = 124. Check: 124 × 10 = 1024 = 512.

items.q: Which multiplication checks that 34 ÷ 38 = 2?
c: 34 × 38
items.e: Answer × divisor should give the number you started with: 2 × 38 = 68 = 34.

items.q: The model shows 36 kg split into 4 equal units. Find 34 of 36 kg.
items.e: 4 units = 36 kg. 1 unit = 36 kg ÷ 4 = 9 kg. 3 units = 3 × 9 kg = 27 kg.

items.q: The model shows 27 litres split into 3 equal units. Find 23 of 27 litres.
items.e: 3 units = 27 litres. 1 unit = 27 litres ÷ 3 = 9 litres. 2 units = 2 × 9 litres = 18 litres.

items.q: The model shows 56 m split into 8 equal units. Find 58 of 56 m.
items.e: 8 units = 56 m. 1 unit = 56 m ÷ 8 = 7 m. 5 units = 5 × 7 m = 35 m.

items.q: Find 38 of 96 kg.
items.e: 8 units = 96 kg. 1 unit = 96 kg ÷ 8 = 12 kg. 3 units = 3 × 12 kg = 36 kg.

items.q: Find 49 of 54 m.
items.e: 9 units = 54 m. 1 unit = 54 m ÷ 9 = 6 m. 4 units = 4 × 6 m = 24 m.

items.q: Find 710 of 250 g.
Find 27 of 84 cm.
items.e: 7 units = 84 cm. 1 unit = 84 cm ÷ 7 = 12 cm. 2 units = 2 × 12 cm = 24 cm.

items.q: Find the value of 512 × 96.
items.e: 512 × 96 means 512 of 96. 12 units = 96. 1 unit = 96 ÷ 12 = 8. 5 units = 5 × 8 = 40.

items.q: Find the value of 35 × 85.
items.e: 35 × 85 means 35 of 85. 5 units = 85. 1 unit = 85 ÷ 5 = 17. 3 units = 3 × 17 = 51.

items.q: Find 25 of 1 h. Give your answer in minutes.
items.e: 1 h = 60 min. 1 unit = 60 min ÷ 5 = 12 min. 2 units = 2 × 12 min = 24 min. (1 h is 60 min, not 100 min.)

items.q: Find 38 of 1 kg. Give your answer in grams.
Find 56 of 3 litres. Give your answer in millilitres.
Find 35 of 2 m 50 cm. Give your answer in centimetres.
items.e: 2 m 50 cm = 250 cm. 1 unit = 250 cm ÷ 5 = 50 cm. 3 units = 3 × 50 cm = 150 cm. (Do not leave out the 50 cm.)

items.q: There are 48 pupils in the school hall. 58 of them are girls. How many boys are there?
items.e: The girls are 5 units out of 8, so the boys are 3 units. 1 unit = 48 ÷ 8 = 6. Boys: 3 × 6 = 18. (30 is the number of girls.)

items.q: Mr Rahman had 48 m of rope. He used 38 of it to tie up a tent and 14 of it to make a fence for a garden bed. How much more rope did he use for the tent than for the fence?
items.e: 38 of 48 m = 18 m. 14 of 48 m = 12 m. Difference: 18 m − 12 m = 6 m. (You can also subtract first: 38 − 14 = 18, and 18 of 48 m = 6 m.)

items.q: There are 40 pupils in a Primary 6 class. 35 of them take the bus to school and 14 of them walk. How many more pupils take the bus than walk?
items.e: 35 of 40 pupils = 24 pupils. 14 of 40 pupils = 10 pupils. Difference: 24 pupils − 10 pupils = 14 pupils. (You can also subtract first: 35 − 14 = 720, and 720 of 40 pupils = 14 pupils.)

items.q: A school garden has an area of 90 m². 25 of it is grass and 13 of it is flower beds. How much greater is the area of grass than the area of flower beds?
items.e: 25 of 90 m² = 36 m². 13 of 90 m² = 30 m². Difference: 36 m² − 30 m² = 6 m². (You can also subtract first: 25 − 13 = 115, and 115 of 90 m² = 6 m².)

items.q: Ada ate 38 of a cake and her brother ate 16 of the same cake. How much more of the cake did Ada eat than her brother?
items.e: Use a common denominator: 38 = 924 and 16 = 424. 924 − 424 = 524. (Rename both fractions before you subtract.)

items.q: Gbenga has 34 as many stamps as Kayode. Kayode has 18 more stamps than Gbenga. How many stamps do they have altogether?
items.e: Gbenga has 3 units and Kayode has 4 units. The difference is 1 unit = 18. Altogether: 3 + 4 = 7 units = 7 × 18 = 126 stamps.

items.q: The mass of Box A is 58 of the mass of Box B. The total mass of the two boxes is 39 kg. What is the mass of Box A?
items.e: Box A has 5 units and Box B has 8 units: 13 units altogether. 13 units = 39 kg, 1 unit = 3 kg. Box A: 5 × 3 kg = 15 kg.

items.q: Mr Bello had 120 mandarin oranges. He gave 14 of them to his neighbours and 23 of the remainder to his relatives. How many mandarin oranges did he have left?
items.e: Neighbours: 14 of 120 = 30. Remainder: 120 − 30 = 90. Relatives: 23 of 90 = 60. Left: 90 − 60 = 30.

items.q: Mrs Eze had a roll of ribbon 72 m long. She used 58 of it to wrap gift boxes and 13 of the remainder to make bows. How many metres of ribbon did she use to make bows?
items.e: Gift boxes: 58 of 72 m = 45 m. Remainder: 72 m − 45 m = 27 m. Bows: 13 of 27 m = 9 m. (Take 13 of the remainder, not of 72 m.)

items.q: Gbenga had 84 stickers. He gave 27 of them to his sister and 35 of the remainder to his friends. How many stickers did he give to his friends?
items.e: Sister: 27 of 84 = 24. Remainder: 84 − 24 = 60. Friends: 35 of 60 = 36. (Take 35 of the remainder, not of 84.)

items.q: A tank had 96 litres of water. 38 of the water was used to wash a car and 25 of the remainder was used to water the plants. How much water was left in the tank?
items.e: Car: 38 of 96 litres = 36 litres. Remainder: 96 litres − 36 litres = 60 litres. Plants: 25 of 60 litres = 24 litres. Left: 60 litres − 24 litres = 36 litres.

items.q: There were 450 people at a National Day concert. 25 of them were adults and 13 of the remainder were boys. The rest were girls. How many girls were there?
items.e: Adults: 25 of 450 = 180. Remainder: 450 − 180 = 270. Boys: 13 of 270 = 90. Girls: 270 − 90 = 180.

items.q: Mrs Okafor baked 144 meat pies. She sold 512 of them in the morning and 37 of the remainder in the afternoon. How many meat pies did she sell in the afternoon?
items.e: Morning: 512 of 144 = 60. Remainder: 144 − 60 = 84. Afternoon: 37 of 84 = 36. (Take 37 of the remainder, not of 144.)

items.q: A drinks stall sold 240 drinks on Saturday. 38 of them were bubble tea and 15 of the remainder were kopi. How many cups of kopi were sold?
items.e: Bubble tea: 38 of 240 = 90. Remainder: 240 − 90 = 150. Kopi: 15 of 150 = 30. (Take 15 of the remainder, not of 240.)

items.q: Blessing had 150 beads. She used 35 of them to make a necklace and 23 of the remainder to make a bracelet. How many beads did she use altogether?
items.e: Necklace: 35 of 150 = 90. Remainder: 150 − 90 = 60. Bracelet: 23 of 60 = 40. Altogether: 90 + 40 = 130.

items.q: Temi had 3 h of free time on Saturday. She spent 14 of the time reading and 23 of the remaining time at the swimming pool. How much free time did she have left? Give your answer in minutes.
items.e: 3 h = 180 min. Reading: 14 of 180 min = 45 min. Remainder: 180 − 45 = 135 min. Swimming: 23 of 135 min = 90 min. Left: 135 − 90 = 45 min.

items.q: Ngozi had 1 litre 500 ml of orange juice. She poured 15 of it into a glass and 25 of the remainder into a bottle. How much juice was left? Give your answer in millilitres.
items.e: 1 litre 500 ml = 1,500 ml. Glass: 15 of 1,500 ml = 300 ml. Remainder: 1,500 − 300 = 1,200 ml. Bottle: 25 of 1,200 ml = 480 ml. Left: 1,200 − 480 = 720 ml.

items.q: 27 of the pupils in a Primary 6 class wear spectacles. 12 pupils wear spectacles. How many pupils are there in the class?
items.e: 2 units = 12 pupils. 1 unit = 12 pupils ÷ 2 = 6 pupils. The whole is 7 units: 7 × 6 pupils = 42 pupils.

items.q: Mr Yusuf has read 58 of a book. He has read 150 pages. How many pages are there in the book?
items.e: 5 units = 150 pages. 1 unit = 150 pages ÷ 5 = 30 pages. The whole is 8 units: 8 × 30 pages = 240 pages.

items.q: A tank is 38 full. It has 24 litres of water in it. What is the capacity of the tank?
items.e: 3 units = 24 litres. 1 unit = 24 litres ÷ 3 = 8 litres. The whole is 8 units: 8 × 8 litres = 64 litres.

items.q: Yusuf gave away 59 of his marbles and had 28 marbles left. How many marbles did he have at first?
items.e: 59 was used, so 9 − 5 = 4 units are left. 4 units = 28 marbles, 1 unit = 7 marbles. At first: 9 units = 9 × 7 marbles = 63 marbles. (28 marbles is the part left, not the part used.)

items.q: After 38 of the water in a tank was used, 45 litres of water was left. How much water was in the tank at first?
items.e: 38 was used, so 8 − 3 = 5 units are left. 5 units = 45 litres, 1 unit = 9 litres. At first: 8 units = 8 × 9 litres = 72 litres. (45 litres is the part left, not the part used.)

items.q: A fruit seller sold 712 of his durians and had 40 durians left. How many durians did he have at first?
items.e: 712 was used, so 12 − 7 = 5 units are left. 5 units = 40 durians, 1 unit = 8 durians. At first: 12 units = 12 × 8 durians = 96 durians. (40 durians is the part left, not the part used.)

items.q: In the model, 3 of the 8 equal units have a value of 27. What is the value of the whole bar?
items.e: 3 units = 27. 1 unit = 27 ÷ 3 = 9. The whole bar is 8 units: 8 × 9 = 72.

items.q: In the model, 3 of the 5 equal units have a value of 51. What is the value of the whole bar?
items.e: 3 units = 51. 1 unit = 51 ÷ 3 = 17. The whole bar is 5 units: 5 × 17 = 85.

items.q: In the model, the 4 white units have a value of 32. What is the value of the whole bar?
items.e: 4 units = 32. 1 unit = 32 ÷ 4 = 8. The whole bar is 7 units: 7 × 8 = 56.

items.q: In the model, the 7 white units have a value of 49. What is the value of the whole bar?
items.e: 7 units = 49. 1 unit = 49 ÷ 7 = 7. The whole bar is 9 units: 9 × 7 = 63.
